classification.difficultyReason: Identifies the sphere radius and checks the standard volume formula using a supplied polynomial integral.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Consider the region bounded by the curve $y=\sqrt{9-x^2}$ and the $x$-axis between $x=-3$ and $x=3$.

spec.description: Unshaded upper semicircle with equal coordinate scales and both-ended axes.
spec.mathematics: y=sqrt(9-x^2), -3<=x<=3; endpoints (-3,0),(3,0), maximum (0,3). Horizontal labels -4 through 4 excluding zero; vertical labels -1,1,2,3,4.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph is visible in every edition.

children.label: b
children.prompt:
When this region is rotated about the $x$-axis, a sphere is formed.

Find the radius of the sphere and hence find its volume using $V=\frac43\pi r^3$.

answer.worked:
The semicircle has radius $3$, so the sphere has radius $r=3$ units.
$$\begin{align*}V&=\frac43\pi r^3\\V&=\frac43\pi(3^3)\\V&=36\pi\text{ units}^3\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\pi\int_{-3}^3(9-x^2)\,dx&=\pi\left[9x-\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_{-3}^3\\&=\pi\left(\left(27-9\right)-\left(-27+9\right)\right)\\&=\pi(18+18)\\&=36\pi\text{ units}^3\end{align*}$$
This agrees with the sphere formula.
